rationale: From ϫⲁⲕ/ϫⲱⲕ 'edge, completion, tip.' Used in this kephalaion (lines 27, 32) for the topmost extremity of the body (the hair-bearing crown of the head) and as the subject of 'they grow' (ⲯⲁⲩⲣⲱⲧ) — the painlessly-cut tips that regenerate. Distinguishes the cuttable extremities from the painful interior 'members' (ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ).

Possibly verbal noun on ⲡⲱⲧ 'run' (giving 'the running' as activity), or alternatively ⲡⲉⲡ-ⲡⲁⲧ 'the foot' (with reduplicated article + Lyc ⲡⲁⲧ 'foot, knee'). Context (line 8: 'mercy that you do there with the X there') is too fragmentary to decide; the agricultural/ascetic register of catechumens' good works admits either reading. Confidence low.

Numerical chapter-marker (ⲣ̄=100, ⲓⲉ̄=15). Appears three times around the chapter title on this page in an ornamental triple-marking pattern characteristic of this manuscript witness. Should be tagged as a structural/numeric marker rather than translated as text.

In this section (lines 21-33) the character ⲯ is used systematically for what would normally be ϣ in standard Coptic orthography. This affects: ⲯⲁⲛ (= ϣⲁⲛ 'when'), ⲯⲱⲱⲧ (= ϣⲱⲱⲧ 'cut'), ⲯⲱⲛⲉ (= ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'be sick'), ⲯⲁⲩ (= ϣⲁⲩ 'habitual'), ⲯⲱⲃ (= ϣⲱⲃ/ϣⲱⲱⲃ 'shave/trim'), ⲯⲁⲣⲉ (= ϣⲁⲣⲉ 'habitual'). Documented as a scribal feature for future pages of the same manuscript.
